title: Orange chocolate truffles
subtitle: dark ganache truffles with fresh orange zest and a hint of warmth
excerpt: Orange and dark chocolate is one of the classic British sweet combinations. These truffles use fresh orange zest stirred into the warm ganache, which releases the citrus oils and gives a much cleaner flavour than orange extract. A small amount of unsalted butter adds gloss and rounds off the bitterness.
sourceNotes: Orange and dark chocolate truffle, a British confectionery staple. Ganache truffle method from standard British patisserie practice; orange-chocolate pairing widely documented from the early twentieth century.

glossaryTerms.definition: A smooth emulsion of chocolate and hot cream. The ratio of chocolate to cream determines whether the ganache is used as a glaze, a filling, or a rolled truffle.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze uncoated in a single layer, then transfer to a freezer bag. Defrost overnight in the fridge and roll in cocoa before serving.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keep refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks.

content.text: Fresh orange zest, stirred into the cream before it heats, gives a cleaner orange flavour than extract because the heat extracts the oils from the zest. Use unwaxed oranges if you can, as waxed fruit rinds can have an off flavour when cooked. Use 70% dark chocolate for the best contrast with the sweet citrus.
Finely zest the orange into the double cream in a small saucepan. Heat over a medium heat, stirring, until the cream just reaches the boil. This infuses the citrus oils into the cream as it heats.
Pour the hot cream through a fine sieve over the chopped chocolate in a heatproof bowl to remove the zest. Leave for 2 minutes, then stir from the centre outward until a smooth
Add the butter and stir until fully melted and glossy. Cover the surface with cling film and refrigerate for at least 2 hours until firm.
Sift cocoa powder onto a plate. Scoop pieces of chilled ganache roughly 2 cm across and roll quickly between lightly dusted palms into balls.
Roll each truffle in the cocoa until evenly coated. Transfer to a tray and refrigerate for 30 minutes before serving.

attrs.avoid: Avoid pouring the cream in too fast or stirring before the chocolate has had time to melt.
attrs.fix: Try adding 1 tablespoon of warm cream and stirring gently from the centre outward to recover the emulsion.

attrs.avoid: Avoid skimping on the zest; only the zest, not the juice, carries the bright citrus oils.
attrs.fix: Use the full zest of a large orange. If the flavour is still faint after chilling, zest a little fresh orange directly onto the rolled truffles before the final coat of cocoa.
